edges.description: Each variant class lowers the amount of functional eIF2-GTP-Met-tRNAi ternary complex, by impaired complex assembly or by impaired initiator tRNA binding.
Less ternary complex lowers initiation efficiency and loosens start codon selection.
Low eIF2 activity is read by the cell as the signal the integrated stress response exists to produce, so the response is constitutively shifted on.

Proposed route to the neurological phenotype. Supported by the rescue of neuronal differentiation in patient cells and by microcephaly with increased neuronal death in eif2s3-null zebrafish, but not demonstrated in human brain tissue.

Proposed explanation for why a secretory endocrine cell is affected: cells with a high secretory protein load depend most on intact translation initiation and stress handling. Supported by EIF2S3 expression in the islets and by increased cell death on EIF2S3 knockdown, not by human tissue pathology.

The same reasoning applied to the other high-load secretory tissue: the anterior pituitary expresses EIF2S3 during development and its hormone output declines progressively in reported patients. Weaker than the beta cell edge, which has a cell-death and a progenitor-deficiency result behind it; this arm has expression plus clinical course and no tissue pathology or animal model, so the intermediates are unknown.
Impaired brain growth.
The core neurodevelopmental outcome.
Delay across domains, which is how the impairment presents before an intellectual disability can be assessed.
The motor component specifically, reported severe in one missense patient and mild in another.
Epilepsy in most reported patients. Note that untreated hypoglycaemia is an alternative or additional contributor, which is recorded as a hypothesis rather than asserted here.
Neonatal hypoglycaemia precedes the diabetes in reported patients.
Early-onset insulin-dependent diabetes follows.
Progressive decline of anterior pituitary hormone secretion.
TSH deficiency is one of the reported deficient axes.
Growth hormone deficiency is the other reported axis, and postnatal growth retardation is positive in seven of the eight families in which it was assessed.

Hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, plausibly through gonadotropin deficiency in a hypopituitary patient. The reports describe the features without establishing that route, so the edge is not asserted as direct.
Hypogenitalism, by the same unestablished gonadotropin route.
Reproduces the microcephaly and gives a cellular correlate, increased neuronal death.
edges.limitations: Microcephaly and neuronal death are reproduced; the intellectual disability and epilepsy that dominate the human phenotype are not assessable in this model. It is also a complete knockout, whereas the human disease is caused by partial loss of function, so it may overstate severity.

edges.description: Hyperglycaemia from a deficiency of beta cells and pancreatic progenitors, which supports a developmental rather than apoptotic route to the glucose phenotype.
edges.limitations: The mechanism found here, progenitor deficiency without apoptosis, disagrees with the increased cell death seen on EIF2S3 knockdown in a human pancreatic cell line, and patient fibroblasts showed no apoptosis either. The authors themselves read the discrepancy as tissue-dependent mechanisms. The pituitary arm of the disease is not modelled by this animal at all, which is why this link targets the beta cell node only.

edges.description: Reproduces the molecular lesion, reduced initiator tRNA binding to eIF2, and identifies it as the step the variant breaks.
edges.limitations: A yeast protein carrying the equivalent substitution, not the human protein, and the model reports on molecular function only. It says nothing about any tissue or clinical consequence.
edges.source: Yeast eIF2gamma-I318M model of the human I259M variant

nodes.description: Progressive decline of anterior pituitary peptide hormone secretion, reported as growth hormone and TSH deficiency and as a gradual decline rather than a fixed deficit. The support here is weaker than for the beta cell node: it rests on EIF2S3 expression in the developing human pituitary plus the clinical course, with no pituitary tissue from a patient examined and no animal model of the pituitary arm.

nodes.description: Hemizygous missense variants and a recurrent C-terminal frameshift in EIF2S3. Missense variants cluster in the conserved guanine nucleotide binding domain of eIF2gamma; the frameshift p.Ile465Serfs*4 truncates the C-terminus. The two classes reach the same endpoint by different routes, which is why the entry separates them: the C-terminal lesion impairs CDC123-dependent assembly of the eIF2 complex, while domain missense variants impair Met-tRNA binding or subunit contact.

nodes.description: Reduced global protein synthesis together with relaxed stringency of start codon selection, so initiation occurs more often at near-cognate non-AUG codons. Both were measured in yeast models of patient variants and in human cells overexpressing the mutant subunit. The gene-specific component matters as much as the global one: ATF4 and GCN4, whose translation is controlled by eIF2 availability, are derepressed.

nodes.description: The integrated stress response acts by lowering eIF2 activity, so a genetic lesion that lowers it leaves the response partly engaged at baseline and over-engaged under stress. Patient fibroblasts carrying the frameshift show increased stress-response activity, and ATF4 translation is derepressed when the mutant subunit is expressed in human cells. The consequence is reduced tolerance of cellular stress rather than a discrete second disease.

nodes.description: Failure of the insulin-secreting beta cell, giving neonatal hypoglycaemia first and insulin-dependent diabetes later. See the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion; this node does not assert either route.
